text:
Forensic findings
1) Domain context: Residential rental housing involves independent property owners who set lease terms autonomously. Standard practice includes public listings on platforms like Zillow and Apartments.com, where rents are visible and competitive. Property managers typically handle tenant screening, rent collection, and maintenance independently. Legitimate coordination occurs through industry associations focused on property management best practices, regulatory compliance, and market data analysis. Ordinary controls include independent pricing decisions, transparent advertising, and no communication channels dedicated to competitors discussing pricing strategies. Market data from sources like the Census Bureau and local housing authorities provides publicly available rent benchmarks that individual landlords reference separately when setting their own rates.

2) What occurred: The actor created a dedicated communication channel (identified as a private messaging group with the generic descriptor "Market Sync") that included named accounts representing multiple competing property managers. The actor drafted a document titled "Q3 Strategy Notes" containing fields for "neighborhood assignments" where specific geographic areas were allocated to named accounts. The actor populated a spreadsheet with columns for "account_id", "assigned_area", "target_rate_floor", and "deviation_penalty_protocol". The actor sent a message in the channel stating that any named account setting rates below the "target_rate_floor" would trigger the "deviation_penalty_protocol", which referenced coordinated non-renewal of leases for tenants transferring from underpriced units. The actor subsequently sent a message titled "Comms protocol update" instructing participants to use encrypted messaging outside the main channel for future pricing discussions, with instructions to delete messages after reading.

3) Materials/access observed: The actor accessed the private messaging group "Market Sync" containing five named account holders. The actor authored the "Q3 Strategy Notes" document stored in a shared cloud drive folder with the descriptor "Operational Planning". The actor created and maintained the spreadsheet containing the "target_rate_floor" and "deviation_penalty_protocol" fields. The actor had access to the encrypted messaging channel used for subsequent pricing discussions, which was separate from the main coordination group. The actor's named account had administrative permissions over the shared drive folder.

4) Indicators & artifacts: The "Market Sync" private messaging group with competitor participants. The "Q3 Strategy Notes" document containing "neighborhood assignments" and "target_rate_floor" fields. The spreadsheet with "account_id", "assigned_area", "target_rate_floor", and "deviation_penalty_protocol" columns. Messages in the main channel referencing coordinated lease non-renewal as penalty for pricing deviations. The separate encrypted messaging channel established for pricing discussions with auto-deletion instructions. The cloud drive folder "Operational Planning" containing strategy documents accessible only to named competitor accounts. Timestamps showing document creation preceded coordinated rent increases of 8-12% across all assigned areas within a 14-day window.
